entry.title: Build A Reasoning Model From Scratch 7: Reinforcement Learning 2 (Tracking, KL Terms, And More)

media:group.media:title: Build A Reasoning Model From Scratch 7: Reinforcement Learning 2 (Tracking, KL Terms, And More)
media:group.media:description:
This second video on reinforcement learning adds clipped policy rations, a KL loss term, format rewards, and analyzes various training metrics. Plus, it gives additional paper references for more tips and tricks.

media:group.media:title: How LLM self-refinement works
media:group.media:description:
Self-refinement asks an LLM to generate an answer, critique it, and use that critique to revise its response. Here, I walk through the process with a simple math example.
An excerpt from my reasoning model series: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kh9mqTzjuEQ&list=PLfrHAQCRxtUs&index=1

entry.title: How majority voting works for LLMs

media:group.media:title: How majority voting works for LLMs
media:group.media:description:
Generate several responses to the same prompt, then select the most frequent final answer. I walk through a simple example and explain why this is easier for numeric answers than for free-form text.
An excerpt from my reasoning model series: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kh9mqTzjuEQ&list=PLfrHAQCRxtUs&index=1

media:group.media:title: How top-p filters tokens
media:group.media:description:
Top-p sampling keeps the most likely tokens until their cumulative probability reaches a chosen threshold. I walk through an example with p = 0.8, then renormalize the retained probabilities so they sum to one.
An excerpt from my reasoning model series: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kh9mqTzjuEQ&list=PLfrHAQCRxtUs&index=1

entry.title: Where verifiable rewards for reasoning model training come from

media:group.media:title: Where verifiable rewards for reasoning model training come from
media:group.media:description:
A calculator gives us a reference answer to check an LLM’s response. In this example, a matching final answer receives a reward of 1, and a mismatch receives 0.
An excerpt from my reasoning model series: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kh9mqTzjuEQ&list=PLfrHAQCRxtUs&index=1

entry.title: How tokenizers turn text into numbers

media:group.media:title: How tokenizers turn text into numbers
media:group.media:description:
A tokenizer splits text into tokens and maps them to numeric IDs. I walk through this process with the Qwen3 tokenizer, then show how decoding reconstructs the original text.
An excerpt from my reasoning model series: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kh9mqTzjuEQ&list=PLfrHAQCRxtUs&index=1

media:group.media:title: Why learn with "from-scratch" code?
media:group.media:description:
Diagrams help us understand an idea. Implementing it in code makes the details explicit and gives us something we can run and test.
An excerpt from my reasoning model series: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kh9mqTzjuEQ&list=PLfrHAQCRxtUs&index=1

entry.title: What is the relationship between LLMs, Reasoning Models, and Agent Harnesses?

media:group.media:title: What is the relationship between LLMs, Reasoning Models, and Agent Harnesses?
media:group.media:description:
The reasoning model is the engine, and the agent harness is the software around it. Using a go-kart analogy, I explain how they fit together and why understanding the underlying LLM still matters.
An excerpt from my reasoning model series: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kh9mqTzjuEQ&list=PLfrHAQCRxtUs&index=1
Article on coding an agent harness: https://magazine.sebastianraschka.com/p/components-of-a-coding-agent

entry.title: Do Looped Transformers Hide Chain of Thought?

media:group.media:title: Do Looped Transformers Hide Chain of Thought?
media:group.media:description:
Looped transformers reuse the same layers for additional computation. In this clip, I discuss why this might lead to a more compact chain of thought, using a math-exam analogy.
An excerpt from my longer video on looped transformers: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KT4n-z_4QJU

entry.title: Build A Reasoning Model From Scratch 4: Inference Scaling 1 (Temperature, Top-p, Self-Consistency)

media:group.media:title: Build A Reasoning Model From Scratch 4: Inference Scaling 1 (Temperature, Top-p, Self-Consistency)
media:group.media:description:
After motivating the use cases for inference-time scaling, this video first walks through temperature scaling, top-p filtering, and multinomial sampling to generate diverse answers with an LLM. Then, using these techniques, we implement self-consistency to improve LLM answer accuracy.

entry.title: Different Tokens, Different Compute in LLMs

media:group.media:title: Different Tokens, Different Compute in LLMs
media:group.media:description:
In Mixture-of-Recursions, a learned router decides which tokens continue through additional passes of the same transformer layers. Some tokens take one pass, others two or three.
An excerpt from my longer video on looped transformers: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KT4n-z_4QJU

entry.title: Build A Reasoning Model From Scratch 2: Loading a Base Model, Text Generation, and KV Caching

media:group.media:title: Build A Reasoning Model From Scratch 2: Loading a Base Model, Text Generation, and KV Caching
media:group.media:description:
The second video in the Build A Reasoning Model (From Scratch) series illustrates how to load a pre-trained model, how LLM text generation works, and how to make it more efficient with KV caching. (These are the basics to get started, later videos will revisit text-generation with sampling in more detail.)
